checks: A maximal simplicial cone in a finite complete fan is full-dimensional and its ray generators are a basis. Common ray values force agreement on common faces. If all support rows are nonnegative, each piece lies below the assembled function on every cone, and equality holds on its own cone. The resulting maximum is the support of the finite convex hull of the pieces’ coefficient vectors.

For the converse, let x be any maximizing point at an interior direction u where the support agrees locally with u·v. Perturb u by ±epsilon in each coordinate direction and compare with the linear form of x, obtaining x=v. This works for a singleton or a lower-dimensional polytope as well as a full-dimensional one.

The anchored rows extend first by nonnegative ray combinations in any cone and then by convex combinations of extreme anchored weights. The resulting Minkowski inclusions meet the hypotheses of the accepted hull-section criterion. Lattice completeness rules out additional integer sites.

At h, a fixed positive-t affine perturbation is feasible for all small positive t exactly when the active evaluations are nonnegative. Finitely many inactive rows keep their strict slack. In a signed differentiable path the same row divided by t gives opposite inequalities for the derivative in the two limits. Zero active derivative is sufficient via the signed affine path.

For the specified quadratic path with A_I v=0, active slack is exactly t² A_I w/2, and inactive rows remain strict. This includes identically zero rows and vanishing second-order evaluations. Positive volume persists because positive minimum width is open under uniform support perturbations, and the fixed finite collection of interpolation maps makes the ray-to-uniform-support map continuous.

For a one-site base, cutting the square at x₁+x₂=2−t² with 0<|t|<1 leaves all four cardinal supports equal to one. Its diagonal face is the stated segment with positive length and the diagonal ray value is 2−t². The normal fan has the four cardinal rays and the diagonal ray for t≠0 and is coarser at zero. At t=±1/2 the endpoints are (1,3/4) and (3/4,1), and the diagonal value is 7/4. The cut with linear offset instead has left derivative zero and right derivative −1 in that coordinate.

Checked both raw sources at their recorded digests. fbc069c3d3ebfebf:01 (§1) repeats the same two row systems of 94a1565e143d393e §1 for positive-dimensional polytopes and a common refining fan. It adds no claim beyond that specialization. The signed velocity, quadratic feasibility and turnover material is separately in fbc069c3d3ebfebf §2 and is correctly incorporated here.

dependencies.mapping: The support rows construct each K_z as a nonempty compact convex hull in R^d. The anchored rows imply every Minkowski inclusion on the finite base P, so the accepted equivalence gives the exact hull sections at P.

overlap.comparison: It supplies the anchored-inclusion/hull-section equivalence for arbitrary compact convex fibers. It has no finite fan support-row test, exact local velocity description or turnover example.

It tests strict compact containment at extreme weights and derives ambient exposedness for an exposed fiber point. The fixed-fan result characterizes weak compatibility and individual support convexity by finite rows and permits degenerate fibers.

readability: The turnover example uses a singleton sampled base implicitly. The fan is the four cardinal rays with the first quadrant subdivided by the diagonal ray. At the uncut square that ray is a refinement ray.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The two finite row systems characterize actual sampled support values, and finite slack gives the exact radial, two-sided and quadratic statements. The square cut verifies facet birth at order two.
